name: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning
authors: Lakshya A Agrawal, Shangyin Tan, Dilara Soylu, Noah Ziems, Rishi Khare, Krista Opsahl-Ong, Arnav Singhvi, Herumb Shandilya, Michael J Ryan, Meng Jiang, Christopher Potts, Koushik Sen, Alexandros G. Dimakis, Ion Stoica, Dan Klein, Matei Zaharia, Omar Khattab et al. (lead affiliation: UC Berkeley; also Stanford, Databricks, MIT, Notre Dame, BespokeLabs.ai)
reflection_type: verbal-self-critique (natural-language reflection over sampled execution/evaluation trajectories to diagnose problems and propose prompt edits); combined with population/evolutionary search and a Pareto-frontier candidate-merge (crossover) step
feedback_source: self-generated LLM reflection over rich textual traces, augmented by external-tool / environment feedback exposed in the evaluation metric mu_f (e.g., retrieval-relevant-document feedback, compiler/execution/profiling traces for code) plus the scalar task reward; uses train-set ground-truth labels/metric to score candidates
iteration_structure: population/evolutionary (genetic optimization loop maintaining a candidate pool with ancestry; iterative reflective mutation + system-aware crossover/merge, guided by Pareto-based stochastic candidate selection)
reflection_object: prompt/context — GEPA reflects on action trajectories (reasoning chains, tool calls, tool outputs, evaluation traces) and modifies the natural-language instructions/prompts of each module within a compound AI system; model weights are NOT updated
requires_training: none (no weight updates; GEPA optimizes textual prompt parameters only. Its GRPO baseline uses RL with LoRA, but GEPA itself requires no training)
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge (an LLM performs reflective credit assignment over traces) combined with a verifiable/task evaluation metric (mu) and a feedback function (mu_f) that surfaces environment/tool textual feedback; no separately trained reward model
distillation_target: prompt — accumulated natural-language lessons are distilled into evolved high-level instructions/prompts for each module of the compound AI system (carried along the genetic/ancestry tree of candidates)
emergent_vs_engineered: prompt/scaffold-engineered — reflection is an explicitly engineered optimizer step (reflective mutation meta-prompt + Pareto evolutionary search), not RL-emergent reasoning
memory_type: playbook/cheatsheet (evolved instruction prompts accumulating high-level rules) backed by a population/candidate pool with ancestry tracking; lessons accumulate along the genetic tree
memory_persistence: cross-task (within a single optimization run over a task's training distribution); the resulting optimized prompt then transfers to held-out test instances of that task. Not designed as a cross-session production memory store
memory_curation_mechanism: population-or-Pareto-selected — GEPA maintains an instance-wise Pareto frontier of candidates, prunes strictly dominated candidates, and stochastically samples promising ones; complementary lessons are combined via system-aware merge (crossover), preventing collapse to a single greedy line and escaping local optima
error_localization_granularity: step-level / agent-level (multi-agent) — reflection performs implicit credit assignment that attributes success/failure to specific modules of the compound system (round-robin per-module updates), with module-level feedback when available (e.g., per-hop feedback in multi-hop systems)
intra_task_vs_inter_task: inter-task — GEPA transfers experience across many training instances within a task to evolve a generalizable prompt for held-out instances (it is a task-level optimizer that learns high-level rules from trial and error, rather than refining a single output in-flight)
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: avoidance-only — lessons from failed rollouts inform prompt mutations evaluated in subsequent optimization iterations; GEPA does not correct a trajectory mid-flight, it improves the prompt for future rollouts
task_domains: QA/reasoning (multi-hop), tool-use/retrieval (RAG), instruction-following, decision-making (privacy-aware delegation), math, and code (inference-time code/GPU-kernel optimization)
benchmarks: HotpotQA, IFBench, HoVer, PUPA (the four core tasks); v2 adds AIME-2025 (math) and code optimization tasks (inference-time search, e.g., GPU/NPU kernel code), for six tasks total
headline_result: Across six tasks, GEPA outperforms GRPO (RLVR) by ~6% on average and by up to ~20% (up to 19pp on Qwen3-8B) while using up to 35x fewer rollouts; it also beats the SOTA prompt optimizer MIPROv2 by over 10% (e.g., +12pp accuracy on AIME-2025). In v1 Table 1, Qwen3-8B aggregate: Baseline 48.85, MIPROv2 55.11, GRPO 51.14, GEPA 61.28 (+12.44); GPT-4.1 mini aggregate: Baseline 52.67, MIPROv2 59.71, GEPA 66.97 (+14.29), GEPA+Merge 68.69 (+16.02)
baselines: GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization, RL with verifiable rewards, 24,000 rollouts with LoRA), MIPROv2 (leading DSPy prompt optimizer), and the unoptimized base system; GEPA+Merge (with system-aware crossover) reported as an additional GEPA variant
gains_vs_baseline: vs GRPO: +10% average gain (v1; v2 abstract states ~6pp average), up to 19-20pp (e.g., +19% on HotpotQA Qwen3-8B), with up to 35x fewer rollouts (and matching GRPO's best validation after as few as ~330-1179 rollouts, up to ~78x greater sample efficiency). vs MIPROv2: GEPA wins on every benchmark/model, aggregate +14% vs MIPROv2's +7% (more than double), e.g., +12pp on AIME-2025
compute_cost_profile: Dramatically cheaper than RL: up to 35x fewer rollouts than GRPO (24,000-rollout LoRA baseline); GEPA reaches optimal test performance with ~678 (IFBench), 2,157 (PUPA), 6,438 (HotpotQA), 6,858 (HoVer) rollouts and matches GRPO validation with as few as ~330 rollouts (up to ~78x more sample-efficient). Most GEPA rollouts are spent on candidate validation on the Pareto set, not mutation. Each iteration also incurs extra LLM calls for reflective prompt generation
known_limitations: (1) The boundary between prompt-based and weight-based learning is not well understood; in data-abundant regimes or where large-scale rollouts are feasible, weight updates may outperform prompting. (2) GRPO baseline used LoRA (not full-parameter finetuning) and limited hyperparameter tuning. (3) GEPA optimizes instructions only, omitting few-shot/exemplar optimization. (4) Majority of rollouts spent on candidate validation; Pareto-validation set size and dynamic/subsampled validation under-explored. (5) Operates on fixed model weights (no weight-space adaptation). (6) Open direction: 'feedback engineering' — identifying which traces give the most useful learning signal
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: external-tool/verifier + oracle-label/ground-truth — GEPA depends on a task evaluation metric mu (with train-set labels/ground truth) to score candidates and on a feedback function mu_f surfacing environment/tool textual feedback (retrieval relevance, compiler/execution traces); reflection is not purely intrinsic. Improvement signal comes from real metric/reward, not unaided self-judgment
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive — using verifiable metric feedback plus reflective credit assignment, GEPA reliably improves over baselines, MIPROv2, and GRPO across all six tasks; gains are validated on held-out test sets, indicating genuine generalization rather than label leakage (test set held out during optimization)
calibration_effect: not-measured (the paper reports task accuracy/performance, not confidence calibration of the underlying model)
failure_attribution_capability: attributes-failing-step — via reflective credit assignment, GEPA implicitly attributes final-outcome success/failure to specific modules/steps of the compound system to target prompt updates; not a dedicated failure-taxonomy classifier
failure_mode_addressed: Targets sample inefficiency and sparse-scalar-reward credit-assignment limits of RLVR/GRPO, and the local-optima/premature-convergence failure of greedy prompt optimizers (addressed via Pareto-based illumination and system-aware merge to avoid getting stuck on one dominant strategy)
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new benchmark dataset released; benchmark suite (HotpotQA, IFBench, HoVer, PUPA, AIME-2025, code tasks) is largely drawn from prior work (Tan et al. 2025 / LangProBe). Open-source GEPA optimizer code and search-tree artifacts released at https://github.com/gepa-ai/gepa
builds_on: GRPO (Shao et al. 2024) as the RL comparison; MIPROv2 (Opsahl-Ong et al. 2024) and DSPy as prior prompt optimizers; evolutionary/self-referential prompt evolution (PromptBreeder, Fernando et al. 2024; EvoPrompt, Guo et al. 2024); MAP-Elites/Pareto 'illumination' (Mouret & Clune 2015); compound-AI-system optimization (Optimas, Wu et al. 2025); LangProBe benchmark suite (Tan et al. 2025)
extended_by_or_inspired: Multi-module GRPO / 'Composing Policy Gradients and Prompt Optimization for Language Model Programs' (Ziems et al., arXiv:2508.04660; AI & Agentic Systems 2026); 'Automatically Learning Skills for Coding Agents' (Tan et al. 2026); optimize_anything: A Universal API for Optimizing any Text Parameter (Agrawal et al. 2026); Combee: Scaling Prompt Learning for Self-Improving Language Model Agents (Li et al. 2026); integration as the GEPA optimizer in DSPy and Meta's llama-prompt-ops
reasoning_model_native: partially — GEPA is model-agnostic and is evaluated with reasoning-capable models (Qwen3-8B with thinking, GPT-4.1 mini) and on reasoning tasks (AIME-2025), but it operates externally by evolving prompts rather than relying on a model's built-in o1/R1-style reflection; reflection is performed by an LLM as an optimizer step, not emergent within the target policy
on_policy_distillation_link: Related but distinct: GEPA distills lessons from on-policy sampled trajectories into prompts (textual policy improvement) rather than into weights; authors explicitly position it against on-policy RL (GRPO) and suggest future hybrid work using GEPA's language lessons to guide RL rollouts, unifying prompt- and weight-based adaptation (cf. Multi-module GRPO follow-up)
sample_efficiency: Very high: up to 35x fewer rollouts than GRPO (24,000-rollout LoRA baseline) to exceed it; matches GRPO's best validation with as few as ~330-1179 rollouts (up to ~78x greater sample efficiency); reaches optimal test performance with ~678 (IFBench) to ~6,858 (HoVer) rollouts
